name: AASIST (Interspeech 2022) ASVspoof2019-LA anti-spoofing
limitations: Checkpoint is not committed; run scripts/fetch_aasist.py to download AASIST.pth (~1.3 MB) into models/aasist.pth.

AASIST code and weights are MIT-licensed (NAVER Corp.) but the model was trained on ASVspoof2019-LA, whose dataset terms are research-oriented; treat the checkpoint as research-use, not a redistributed asset of this repo.
Trained on ASVspoof2019 LA attacks (TTS/VC): generalization to newer neural codecs and commercial voice-clone services is not guaranteed — a low score is not evidence of real audio.
Only the first ~30s is scored, in ~4s windows whose logits are averaged; very long files are not fully covered.
Scores are a prioritization signal, not a truth label.
notes: Runtime 'aasist' delegates to scripts/run_aasist.py, a faithful reimplementation of clovaai/aasist models/AASIST.py (sinc-conv front-end + 6 residual blocks + spectro-temporal graph attention); attribute names match the official state dict.

Audio is decoded to mono at sample_rate, then scored in non-overlapping evenly-spaced windows of window_samples (64600 ~= 4.04s, the upstream evaluation cut); windows beyond the file are skipped and short files are loop-padded exactly like upstream pad().
Model logits are (spoof=0, bonafide=1) — upstream's own eval reads index 1 as the bonafide score, so score_index 0 with softmax yields the spoof/fake probability on a 0-100 scale.
The checkpoint path is relative to this profile's directory (models/); keep it out of git — it is covered by .gitignore.
